To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the crystallization of Fab fragments can be improved by using engineered mutants of the protein L domain.

we have designed PpL mutants that have different binding characteristics, that we have used these mutants to crystallize light chain fragments and that we have determined the structure of these complexes.
the crystallization of immunoglobulin fragments can be improved by using engineered variants of the protein L, that have been mutated in their binding site to the light chain.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the design of IBPs with different properties and with the analysis of the packing modes obtained in the crystals of antibody complexes with these IBPs.
the engineering of IBPs and the characterization of their binding properties.
the development of a new approach to protein crystallization based on the use of IBP mutants and their ability to crystallize with antibody fragments.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
PpL mutants can be useful for crystallization of antibody and Fab fragments.
the use of PpL mutants can be useful for the crystallization process, but it is difficult to predict which mutant would be the best choice in each case.
the PpL mutant selection is not a trivial task.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have been successful in designing and engineering mutants that can be used in crystallization of immunoglobulin light chains, and in particular, in the crystallization of the Fab fragment of an anti-idiotype antibody.
the use of IBP mutants can expand the range of lattics available for antibody fragment crystallization.
the use of PpL mutants can be a powerful tool to obtain crystals of antibody fragments.
The main takeaway from our work is that
IBP domains can be engineered for specific crystallization properties.
IBP mutants can be used as a general tool for the crystallization and structure determination of antibody fragments.
PpL mutants can be designed with altered binding properties and that these properties can be used to modify crystal lattice packing modes.
